title: Friends remember Westmount shooting victim as a 'nice, decent guy'
article: A man fatally shot by police Saturday in the Westmount McDonald's parking lot had been in a downward spiral since his fraternal twin Mitch Dumas died by suicide in 2011, said a high school friend from Drayton Valley Sunday.

Brittany Larson remembers Matt Dumas, 30, as a "nice, decent guy" who was funny and fun to be around. Larson said he was always laughing until Mitch Dumas died. Shortly after, Matt Dumas left Drayton Valley and found himself in trouble.
Larson said Dumas had young children.
Edmonton police were attempting to arrest a suspect on outstanding warrants Saturday night when officers opened fire, leaving a man dead.
In a statement Sunday morning, police said officers tried to arrest the suspect near Westmount Mall, but he rammed a police cruiser with his vehicle while attempting to flee the scene.
"A confrontation then occurred between the male suspect and officers, and the officers subsequently discharged their service weapons," the statement reads.
The 30-year-old was pronounced dead at the scene, where police also recovered a handgun.
No officers were hurt.
The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT), which investigates officer-involved shootings, said it is looking into the incident.

Police remained on the scene Sunday morning in an area of the parking lot taped off in front of the McDonald's. Several unmarked police vehicles surrounded a silver Mercedes with 11 visible bullet holes in the front windshield.
Witnesses said they heard the gunfire around 8:15 p.m.
Jeramie Wigelsworth, who lives directly across the street, was watching a movie with his girlfriend when they heard a loud bang.
"My girlfriend walked up to the door, heard another bang and it was loud," he said. "She looked out the window and saw gunfire and dropped down."
The parking lot outside the McDonald's was blocked off, Wigelsworth said, by a "full army" of police noting about 30 vehicles in total.
Wigelsworth said the first bang they heard was a different sound than the gunfire that followed.
"There was a distinct explosion-type sound," he said.
Edmonton friend Shelby Orr described Dumas as an "open door" kind of a guy who gave everyone a chance and helped out whenever he could.
Orr said Dumas struggled with drug issues, but said he was still a human being and that she is in tears over his death.
Another friend from Edmonton, Bane Derekson described him as a loving.

"He was one of the most loving people that I have had the privilege to meet and he was always there for everybody even when they weren't there for him. He will be missed dearly by both his friends and his family," Derekson said.
Witnesses said they heard the gunfire around 8:15 p.m. Saturday.
The parking lot outside the McDonald's was blocked off, Wigelsworth said, by a "full army" of police, seeing about 30 vehicles in total.
Two other people, a man and a woman, were arrested on the scene and Wigelsworth said they were surrounded by police and lying on their stomachs.
Jacob Rothenburger was having a coffee in his car, checking his phone to hear from a friend, when he heard three massive bangs that "reverberated."
When he looked up, he saw unmarked police vehicles boxing in a Mercedes, which was attempting to back up.
The next thing he heard was about 15 gunshots.
"Pop, pop, pop," he said, describing the noise. "I was just shaking."
Later Saturday night, police went to houses across the street to check on residents and ask them to look on their property for any debris, Wigelsworth said.
ASIRT has not provided any further information Sunday.
